subject: Unexpected usage surplus on Jan invoice (INV-OMC-202701) - request for clarification
messages:
From: Eve Barnes <accounts@omnicart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Gareth O'Neil <gareth@omnicart.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T09:14:00Z
Subject: Invoice INV-OMC-202701 - large token delta vs expected

Hi Marcus,

We received invoice INV-OMC-202701 this morning and the token usage line shows ~2,600,000 tokens for January. Our internal monitoring indicates roughly 1.1–1.3M tokens for the same period (same API key + app traffic). Attached is a CSV export from our telemetry (omnicart_usage_export_202701.csv) with timestamps and request_ids.

Can you explain why your metering shows more than double what we're seeing? This is a material difference for our month-end close — our procurement has put payment on hold pending resolution.

Two specific asks:
- Please provide the raw usage export you used to generate the invoice (timestamped token counts by request_id or session).
- Confirm VAT treatment for this invoice: OmniCart (EU entity) expects reverse-charge handling; if you reissue a corrected invoice we need the VAT details for our records.

Thanks,
Eve Barnes
Head of Finance — OmniCart
accounts@omnicart.com
+44 20 7XX XXX XXX

Attachment: omnicart_usage_export_202701.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Barnes <accounts@omnicart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-18T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Invoice INV-OMC-202701 - large token delta vs expected

Hi Eve — thanks for the note and the CSV, I appreciate the clear timestamps. I've looped in Kimberly (billing ops) and Ben (finance) to triage immediately.

Short answer: we will pull the same timestamped telemetry and a tokenized export used to produce the invoice. We often see a small delta from streaming vs per-request counting, but the magnitude you report is bigger than expected so we'll run a signal-level reconciliation.

Our next steps (I will coordinate):
1) Kimberly will run a sampling export across your account and check for overlapping session windows, prefetch/replay tags, and any orphaned request replays.
2) We'll compare request_ids (your CSV) to our raw eventlog and provide a side-by-side report.
3) Pending the outcome we'll propose either an invoice correction or a provisional credit so your payment isn't blocked.

Can you confirm the API keys in use for January (or the specific key in the CSV) and whether you ran any bulk replays or embedding backfills in the period 2027-01-06 -> 2027-01-17? That will speed the triage.

I'll aim to update you within 24 hours after the first pass.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-18T14:28:00Z
Subject: Internal: initial triage notes for OmniCart (INV-OMC-202701)

Marcus / Ben — initial findings after pulling a 48h sample around the spike window:
- We observed an aggregation/windowing mismatch for streaming calls where chunked streaming tokens were attributed to both the 'session start' and the 'stream chunk' lines in the billing aggregation job for a subset of sessions. That can double count tokens when sessions cross the hourly boundary.
- There are ~23k request_ids in your CSV that map directly to server-side replays tagged with "replay_batch_v2" on 2027-01-12 02:00 UTC — these were part of an internal backfill run the customer initiated (omnicart reported some reindex work yesterday). If those replay jobs were retried or partially deduped on our ingestion, counts could inflate.
- VAT note: because OmniCart is an EU-registered entity, if we reissue a corrected invoice we need their VAT ID and confirmation of reverse-charge applicability. Reissued invoice must include the original invoice number reference and a zero-VAT line if reverse-charge applies.

Proposed remediation path:
A) Produce a reconciled side-by-side (our tokens vs their exported tokens) with request_id matching. B) If we confirm double-counting, issue a credit and reissue corrected invoice with VAT adjustment. C) If the overage stems from legitimate replay traffic initiated by OmniCart, provide detailed evidence and discuss a one-time exception credit if warranted.

I'll generate the reconciled CSV and include sample lines (omnicart_sample_requests_202701.xlsx). ETA: EOD 2027-01-19 for the first delivery.

Attachment (internal): omnicart_sample_requests_202701.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Barnes <accounts@omnicart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-19T08:31:00Z
Subject: Re: Invoice INV-OMC-202701 - large token delta vs expected

Hi Eve — quick update from our side: thanks for the export. Kimberly completed an initial sample and we identified two likely contributors to the delta: a) replay/backfill jobs on 2027-01-12 that appear in our ingestion window and b) a streaming chunk attribution bug that can double-count when a session straddles the hourly boundary.

To proceed we need two quick confirmations from you:
1) Confirm the API key(s) present in your CSV (you can paste the first 8 chars of the key) so we match the right streams.
2) Please attach your company VAT ID (for reissued invoice / reverse-charge). If you prefer we can accept the VAT certificate PDF.

Proposal to get you unstuck: we will apply a provisional credit of EUR 28,000 on the Jan invoice while we complete the full reconciliation. If the final reconciliation shows a smaller adjustment we'll invoice the net difference, or if it is larger we'll of course correct in your favor. The provisional credit will allow procurement to release payment while we finalize.

If that works, please reply with the API key snippet and attach the VAT doc. We'll treat this as priority and aim to deliver the reconciled CSV and final credit decision by EOD 2027-01-21.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Eve Barnes <accounts@omnicart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Gareth O'Neil <gareth@omnicart.com>
Date: 2027-01-21T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Invoice INV-OMC-202701 - large token delta vs expected

Thanks Marcus — that provisional credit is most helpful.

API key snippet: sk-live-7a3b9f2c (appears as column api_key_prefix in our CSV).
Attached is our VAT certificate (omnicart_vat_certificate_202701.pdf). We did trigger an embedding backfill on 2027-01-12 via the internal tool (confirmed) and there were a few retries due to transient errors. We suspected the replay might affect counts, glad you found the same.

Please proceed with the provisional credit and share the reconciled side-by-side when ready — our procurement needs the corrected invoice + VAT evidence to complete the payment release. Also, can you confirm how you will indicate the reverse-charge on the corrected invoice (line items and reference)? That helps our AP team.

Best,
Eve Barnes
Head of Finance — OmniCart

Attachment: omnicart_vat_certificate_202701.pdf
